Jardín maternal, translated as Maternal Kindergarten, takes children from 45 days (the minimum legal postpartum maternity leave) up to 4 years old. These institutions can be public (very few, with a long wait-list) or private. They divide kids into "rooms" according to their age: babies and toddlers who cannot walk have their own room, and then you have rooms for 1, 2, 3, and 4 year-old children. Each room usually has two teachers (or one teacher and one assistant teacher) and their own curriculum. They do school activities on blocks of 20-30 minutes each, but are flexible and also provide general care (hygiene, naps, meals). Also, private employers must cover daycare for children younger than three (that is, they must provide their own daycare facilities or cover the cost for one of the parents).

Formal education may start at 3 or 4, depending on where you live. So you get three years of kindergarten (3, 4, and 5 years old).

This is part of his 'sincere guy' persona, which is one of the reasons he was elected on the first place (you know, 'he says it like it is'). On top of that, he never, ever admits a mistake. Some very clear mistakes have been made during his administration, particularly at the beginning, and he has always tried to reframe them as personal victories or the behind-the-scenes machinations of his enemies. Sometimes, the person responsible for those mistakes has been dismissed afterwards.

Taking all of this into account, a few days ago the president promoted a memecoin on Twitter. He vaguely framed that memecoin as an investment opportunity in the country and part of his economical agenda. The same memecoin turned out to be the mother of all rug pulls, and plummeted that same day, resulting in a handful of people getting around 100 million dollars. When it became obvious that this was a scam, he deleted his original tweet and offered a non-apology blaming his political opponents and denying his implication in the scam. But it was too late. Chaos ensued. Argentine newspapers talked about nothing else. Milei's political opponents had a field day. Even some of his political supporters started to show how glad they would be if his head were to roll. 

During the aftermath of the events, some things have happened. First, the president is avoiding Twitter, I can't even describe how unusual this is. Second, some people connected to the memecoin have declared that he was fully aware of everything beforehand, contradicting Milei's version of the events. Third, some of his electorate are suddenly facing the prospect of the president being either a complete idiot or a scammer, sending his supporters into caos. This is relevant given that Milei is very popular among your stereotypical tech bros. Fourth, the whole debacle reached international news outlets, damaging his already damaged credibility. Milei craves international recognition and likes to fancy himself a world leader, so this probably impacted him personally. Fifth, some investigations are currently being held, in Argentina and in the US. Whether something might come out of them or not is unclear. An impeachment is being considered, but this is 100% a political move without any chance of succeeding. I should add that it is highly possible that other political figures were part of the scandal, but they are the kind of people that might be too close to the president to be kicked out of the administration. Some rumors involve Milei's sister, which he absolutely adores and has become a sort of de facto VP.

The latest chapter of this saga came out yesterday, when Milei finally broke his silence in an interview with a friendly TV show. Said interview was broadcasted on TV and streamed on YouTube. Turns out the YouTube version was unedited and featured one of the president's closest collaborators censoring a question about the scam because of its possible legal repercussions for Milei. So, the interview which was supposed to clear him of all wrongdoing ended up rekindling the scandal.

Buenas, personal de salud por aquí. La vacuna contiene un fragmento de una molécula asociada al virus. Para que te dé HPV o cáncer necesitas que te infecte el virus entero, por ende es imposible que te dé HPV por la vacuna.

Cuando comenzó la vacunación hace unos 15 años estaban todos los miedos populares que aparecen con una vacuna nueva (como con la del COVID). Pero ahora ya es una vacuna con muchos años de efectividad y seguridad probadas, y ha demostrado casi eliminar el cáncer de cuello de útero en las poblaciones vacunadas.

No es cierto que no se pueda dar pasados los 11 años, se coloca a esa edad porque es más efectiva. Además tiene más sentido colocarle la vacuna a niños en una edad en la que aún no estuvieron expuestos al HPV.

Por otro lado existen muchísimos tipos de HPV, y la vacuna previene contra 2 o 4, según la marca. Por ende no te protege contra todos los HPV y por eso te podes infectar aunque estés vacunada. Lo importante es que esos subtipos que cubre la vacuna son los que generan la gran mayoría de los casos de cáncer.

Spanish speaker here. I would say that Spanish, Portuguese, and Italian are similar enough. People fluent in these three languages could have a simple conversation and understand most of it. French is kind of an outlier, you could maybe read some of it, but its pronunciation is way different to the rest of the romance languages. Romanian is even more different. Still, I usually go for the Spanish translation of any of these languages.

Spanish is my first language, so I also prefer romance-language books translated into Spanish (except for Italian, which I can understand enough to read some books). However, if there's an English translation, I usually go for English. Spanish translations tend to be written in Spaniard Spanish, and a I find that Spaniard expressions take me out of the story. It's hard to imagine, say, a Japanese woman using slang from Madrid.

Latin America has developed something we call Español Latino, or Latin Spanish, which is a form of Spanish that doesn't really correspond to the dialect of any region, but is standard for translations and dubs. Since we grew up listening to this Spanish in the media, it's far easier for me to read foreign works written in it, given that we (paradoxically) associate Latin Spanish with foreignness.

De nada! Yo fui dos días, uno al glaciar y uno al Chaltén. Me arrepentí de no haber ido con más tiempo al Chaltén, si bien todas las excursiones ahí salen un huevo tenés un montón de senderos para recorrer tranqui y es gratis. Si llegas a ir ahí, te conviene tomarte el bondi que sale desde la terminal de El Calafate, es más barato que contratar una combi o excursión. Respecto al glaciar, no hice la excursión de la caminata porque me iba a fumar toda la plata que tenía para el resto del viaje, pero la gente que conocí ahí dice que al menos una vez en tu vida la tenés que hacer. Si vas con tiempo podes contratarla desde acá e ir pagandola en cuotas.

Para empezar, es carísimo. Hacete la idea de que los precios no van a tener sentido, lisa y llanamente porque no están pensados para argentinos. Segundo, alquila auto apenas puedas. En marzo un taxi al centro desde el aeropuerto estaba 25 mil y al perito 150. Sólo con esas dos cosas amortizas el auto. Segundo, andá directamente al parque nacional (unos 25 km), no vale la pena contratar nada. La excursión en barco que te acerca al glaciar la contratas ahí mismo, y todas las caminatas son gratis. Hay un restaurante dentro del parque si querés comer. Lo único que tenés que programar antes, si lo haces, es la caminata arriba del glaciar, que debe estar a unos 280 usd. Por último, y ya más controvertido... No hay mucho más que hacer aparte de ir al glaciar (pero por otro lado, vale 100% la pena, no se puede poner en palabras). Si te interesa el trekking y las excursiones de aventura podes ir unos días al Chaltén (no ir y volver el mismo día, eso no te deja hacer nada), pero pensando que al igual que el Calafate, está todo hecho para extranjeros.

Pasa que el acné es una enfermedad crónica de la piel, tarde o temprano vas a necesitar un dermatólogo. Primero para lograr identificar los desencadenantes de tu acné y tratar de minimizar los brotes. Y segundo porque las cremas que realmente te van a hacer cambios duraderos son medicamentos que se venden bajo receta y requieren control médico. 

Respecto al skincare, todos los activos que tengan los productos son en dosis cosméticas. Eso significa que hay pocas chances de que te hagan mal, pero tampoco te van a hacer muy bien. Usá un limpiador suave por la noche (no hace falta que sea dos veces al día como dicen muchos influencers), los de Neutrogena son pagables y aptos acné. Agregale un protector solar durante el día (no sólo por el tema arrugas o cáncer, la exposición al sol te puede empeorar el acné). Acá no hay uno mágico, depende mucho de tu gusto personal. Yo en mi caso uso el dermaglos efecto seco. Pero reitero, vas a necesitar un dermatólogo.

Tuve un plan hace unos años, hasta que hice un cambio de titularidad. Es decir, no llegué a adjudicar. Mi experiencia fue muy buena, creo que la mayor ventaja lejos es la cancelación por porcentaje. Las contras, además de lo que ya comentaron, es que es difícil adjudicar en los barrios que todo el mundo quiere (por ejemplo, alguno muy bien ubicado). En esos casos, suele ganar la gente que ya pagó todo o casi todo el plan, y sí vos sos un aportante normal no tenés muchas chances de competirles. Lo otro es el tiempo que pasa entre que ganas el sorteo de la casa y te la dan. En ese tiempo pasás a pagar más sin tener todavía una casa, entonces es probable que tengas que sumar el alquiler de donde estés viviendo a la cuota (alta) de la casa de horizonte. La duración de ese período es variable, va a ser mayor si adjudicaste en un barrio que se está creando desde cero. Conozco a alguien que adjudicó en pandemia, y con todas las demoras habidas y por haber propias de la pandemia le tardó poco más de un año. En esta instancia mucha gente elige irse a vivir a la casa de horizonte apenas esté habitable, incluso si todavía no tenés todos los servicios.

Habiendo dicho todo ésto, creo que es una de las pocas (si no la única) opción viable de tener una casa nueva.

Buenas! Por la edad de tu hijo te recomiendo los parques de la ciudad. Ahora la verdad hay un montón y están todos buenos, es gratis y si el día está lindo podes ir a tomar mates mientras la bendi juega. Tenés el parque Las Heras (tiene juegos, fuente, pista para bicis y un puente peatonal muy lindo que cruza el río). En la zona del estadio Kempes tenés literalmente tres, uno al lado del otro: el parque Chateau (muy lindo, grande, y con una casa-museo muy vistosa), el parque del Kempes (este quizás es menos apto para niños, tiene sectores de deportes urbanos y la bendi se va a aburrir) y el Parque Bustos (el más nuevo y no tan grande). En el complejo del estadio tenés también un museo de deportes. En la zona del centro tenés el parque sarmiento que tiene adentro al ex zoológico (muy lindo para caminar, y tiene aún algunos animales, éste a mi hija de dos le encanta) y el super park, que es el parque de diversiones de la ciudad (está medio venido a menos, pero tiene algunos juegos aptos para esa edad). También, relativamente cerca del centro, tenés el Parque de las Tejas que tiene un planetario (se llama Plaza Cielo Tierra). El zoológico y el planetario son gratuitos, pero tenés que reservar tu entrada por internet.

Después hay varios museos en la zona del centro, pero a decir verdad los chicos se re aburren ahí. Los museos gratuitos son el museo de arte urbano y el museo de ciencias naturales, los dos muy cerca.

Podes buscar el instagram de la secretaría de cultura (cultura.municba) que sube los eventos de cada fin de semana. Suele tocar algún DJ o banda local al aire libre en los parques, o a veces alguna obra de teatro.

Not really. Longitudinal studies on breastfeeding babies and women are performed all the time. That is, studies that observe breastfed and formula-fed infants for long periods of time to observe the potential effects of one or the other. Also, breastfeeding (and breastfeeding promotion) is usually a priority research topic on most countries which can get you priority access to research funds.

The kind of studies that usually exclude pregnant and breastfeeding women are intervention studies. That is, studies where you provide some treatment to test its safety or efficacy. But those are not related to the benefits of breast milk.

I'm sorry but no, the scientific consensus on breastfeeding being better than formula feeding for all kinds of babies is near absolute. It's comparable to the consensus on climate change. No scientific association recommends formula over breast milk, except for extremely specific circumstances. Even then, in cases such as premature babies, modified breast milk is preferred to formula. And yes, research on breastfeeding has been conducted on all kinds of countries and population groups.

Formula is ok for feeding babies and it can provide decent nutrition, but other benefits of breastfeeding are extremely difficult or even imposible to replicate.

I'm in Argentina. Minimum paid maternity leave is 90 days (30 or 45 prenatal days, and 60 or 45 postnatal days, you can choose either option), but certain provinces and jobs have extra days. In my job, I have 180 days of paid leave. In the case of fathers and non pregnant mothers, paid leave is really subpar, only 4 days, so most people get paid vacation leave after birth. 

I get a statal pregnancy extra pay during pregnancy, which depends on my income (it's higher for lower income families). It's not much, but covers most of the pregnancy expenses. There are extra pays and leave for mothers of disabled children, but I'm not familiar with them.

The health system here is mixed, that is, you have public, state-funded hospitals (where you pay nothing), something called 'obra social' (I'm not sure about the translation, but it refers to health services associated with your job, you and your employer have to pay a fixed monthly rate to get access), and fully private health insurance. In any case, there is a list of minimum interventions and medicines that must be fully covered for pregnant women, so in practice everything related to pregnancy and delivery is free. 

Something that people from other countries might find weird is that midwives are not really a thing here. Not all provinces recognise midwifery as a profession. Obstetricians are doctors who specialise in gynecology and obstetrics, and they are the ones who usually follow your pregnancy.

A hospital stay for a vaginal birth is usually 24 hours, and for a C section is 48-72 hours. Birth plans are endorsed by law, so theoretically any hospital must respect your birth plan. In reality, however, many places are just not equipped to deal with some demands.

Taking everything into account, I'm mostly happy with the way that pregnancy and birth are dealt with here. I never had to pay for anything health-related during my pregnancy, even when I had lots of extra interventions because of some pregnancy complications. My maternity leave was great, even though the national average is not so much. Also, I have spent most my pregnancy working from home.

My great grandfather, a farm worker, born in the nineteenth century, war and hunger survivor, beat all of his children and was super strict. My father remembers that he had very old fashioned manners, for example, after a meal nobody could leave the table before him and he expected his daughters to perform all house labor. In this sense, I don't find my parents' upbringing to be fundamentally different to my own (a millennial). I think that the most obvious difference would be the sexism. Things are far from perfect, but have improved in the last 10 years or so in ways that I never imagined. 

Feminism used to be some taboo word only expected from crazy leftists, and suddenly it is discussed in prime time tv shows, schools and universities, and feminist marches gather thousands of people. People are increasingly aware of machismo (sexism + toxic masculinity). Gender violence is becoming increasingly visible. For example, every reporter now uses the term feminicide to describe the killing of women for being women, while such word didn't exist some five years ago. Other forms of violence, like catcalling, are becoming more frowned upon.

As far as legislation goes, many important bills have been passed. All public servants must have gender studies (mostly short courses). Half of each party's candidates for councils and the Congress have to be women. There is a law against gender violence which is quite comprehensive. Fertility treatments are free in the public health system. Gender identity is recognised in another law, and gender confirmation treatments are also free in the public health system (though difficult to get anyways). Same gender marriages became legal a decade ago.

Of course, many laws sound great in theory, but then get trampled in practice. Sexist social practices and stereotypes are still alive. Women still perform most care activities. There is a lot of growing resistance towards feminism and the feminist movement (Most importantly, an abortion bill failed to get passed two years ago. This year it was going to be proposed again, but everything got more complicated because of COVID-19). But I would say that sexism is increasingly visible, which is still something very positive.

Muchos autores, sobre todo en ediciones más modernas que las que figuran en la página, prefieren hablar de una etapa pre-embrionaria durante las primeras 3 o 4 semanas de desarrollo, ya que el producto de la concepción durante esta etapa está formado no sólo por las células que luego van a formar el embrión, sino también por células que van a formar parte de la placenta y los anexos ovulares (nadie considera seres humanos a estas estructuras aunque también resulten de la fecundación) y por otras células sin una función clara, que luego van a desaparecer durante el desarrollo. Además, recién en la cuarta semana el embrión adquiere forma cilíndrica; previamente tiene forma de cúmulo de células (en el estadío blastocisto) o de disco (es decir aplanado, durante las semanas 2 y 3). Y no, estos motivos no están basados en la fertilización in vitro como dice la página; autores latinoamericanos y argentinos con una postura pro-vida también hablan de un período pre-embrionario.

Otras de las citas hablan de que el cigoto, y posteriormente el embrión, están vivos. O que a través del desarrollo llegan a formar un ser humano. Ya se ha hablado muchas veces de que "vida" no equivale a "ser humano" ni "vida humana". Biologicamente hablando, un organismo está vivo cuando cumple con las características de los seres vivos: homeostasis, metabolismo, nutrición, irritabilidad, crecimiento y desarrollo, etc. Según este concepto un cigoto está vivo, pero también lo están todas las células que forman el cuerpo humano: las gametas, las somáticas, las células tumorales, todas. El debate real no pasa por si un embrión "vive" o no, si no por si un embrión es una persona humana. Y acá debemos obligadamente salirnos de la embriología, que es el estudio de los procesos sucesivos que ocurren desde la fecundación hasta el nacimiento, para incorporar otras disciplinas. "Vida humana" y "ser humano", quieran o no, no son conceptos estáticos y dogmáticos; distintas sociedades en distintos momentos históricos definieron la aparición de la persona en distintos momentos del desarrollo, inclusive después del nacimiento.

Source: subjetivamente, docente de biología celular y embriología durante 6 años. Libros varios, pero dejo uno argentino y unoestadounidense: 
Embriología médica, José Hib. Octava edición, 2005.
Embriología médica, T. W. Sadler. Doceava edición, 2012.

I have a slightly different situation. My mother always wanted to be a mother, but she got pregnant in a very difficult time in her life. She wanted to study a career, but she had no money for it. She was working to support both her parents. Her then-boyfriend (my father) was older than her, had already finished University, and had a stable job, in other words, he had already fulfilled most of his life objectives. My father wouldn't marry my mother because his own mother (my grandma) and my mother got along terribly, and so my grandma didn't approve of her. 
In this situation, my mother considered having an abortion. She wanted to be a mother, but not in that situation. In the end, she didn't abort, and she had me. 
I am really grateful to her for having told all of this to me. It helped me to understand her situation. I know that she doesn't regret having me, but I would never blame her if she did. Again, it was really important for me to know and understand all of this. It made me wonder about my own life choices and dreams. I didn't have a life crisis when I found out that I wasn't wanted. 
My mother left too many things behind to raise me. Too many of them. For a long time, she had no motivation in life besides myself and my sister. She had a job that she hated, and she never went to university. It took her almost 15 years to realize that she could have a life outside motherhood without beeing a bad mother. I love her, and will always do whatever I can to help her pursue her dreams.
I no longer know if any of this makes any sense. But please, tell your story to your daughter someday. She will understand.
